title: Week Summary: Development, Deployment, and Operational Viewpoints

concepts.name: Development viewpoint
concepts.description: A viewpoint focused on code organization, modules, build structure, dependencies, and development ownership.

concepts.name: Module dependency
concepts.description: A compile-time or build-time relationship where one code module relies on another.

concepts.name: Build unit
concepts.description: A source or package unit that can be built, tested, versioned, or released as part of development.

concepts.name: Dependency rule
concepts.description: An architectural constraint that governs which modules may depend on which other modules.

concepts.name: Deployment viewpoint
concepts.description: A viewpoint focused on mapping software elements to infrastructure, runtime nodes, networks, and environments.

concepts.name: Runtime node
concepts.description: A physical, virtual, or managed environment that hosts software execution or storage.

concepts.name: Deployment environment
concepts.description: A configured setting such as development, staging, production, region, or tenant where software runs.

concepts.name: Infrastructure mapping
concepts.description: The allocation of software elements to compute, storage, network, and managed platform resources.

concepts.name: Operational viewpoint
concepts.description: A viewpoint focused on running, monitoring, supporting, recovering, and changing the live system.

concepts.name: Operational readiness
concepts.description: The degree to which a system can be safely deployed, observed, supported, and recovered in production.

concepts.name: Rollback strategy
concepts.description: A planned way to return a system to a prior safe state after a failed release or configuration change.

concepts.name: Runbook
concepts.description: Operational instructions for routine tasks, incident response, diagnosis, and recovery.
